Tab scope and naming.question: How should the new tab be framed in the UI?
Tab scope and naming.answer: Use an English tab label of "Partners & Projects", with partners first.
options_presented: Projects & Partners - One combined tab matching the roadmap and feedback note; simplest for users and planning.
Partners First - Tab label emphasizes partners, with projects as a secondary section inside it.
Projects First - Tab label emphasizes exemplar projects, with partners supporting them.

Tab scope and naming.question: What should the German tab label be?
options_presented: Partner & Projekte - Short, direct, and matches the English order.
Partner und Projekte - Slightly more formal/readable in German UI.
Praxispartner & Projekte - More specific if these are mostly applied/regional collaboration partners.

Tab scope and naming.question: Inside the tab, should partners and projects be visually separated?
Tab scope and naming.answer: Use two separate sections inside one tab: Partners and Projects.
options_presented: Two Sections - Separate "Partners" and "Projects" headings/panels inside one tab; clearest for mixed content.
Unified List - One combined list with type labels; compact, but can blur the difference.
Map First Only - Emphasize the map and show list details only when a point is selected.

Tab scope and naming.question: Where should this tab sit in the existing tab row?
Tab scope and naming.answer: Place it on the right side of the tab container, visually separated from the existing thematic tabs, rather than simply appending it inline with the current data tabs.
options_presented: After Economic - Add it at the end after the five thematic data tabs; keeps current data-tab order stable.
Before Economic - Put it before the socio-economic tab because it is people/institution-focused.
After Landscape - Keep it near the less technical/contextual tabs.
Freeform: visually separated from the current tabs by being placed on the right side of the tab container.
Inside ll_content.json - Hand-authored alongside existing LL narrative/manager content, then merged into ll_metadata.json; best fit for bilingual static content.
Separate partners_projects.json - Keeps this new content independent from LL descriptive text; cleaner if the list may grow or be maintained separately.
GeoJSON-first - Store points as GeoJSON with properties for names/descriptions; map is natural, but overview content becomes more awkward.
Data authoring model.question: Where should the partner/project entries live?
Data authoring model.answer: Use a separate static file for this content, rather than folding it into ll_content.json.

options_presented: Per-LL grouped JSON - One file keyed by Living Lab slug, e.g. each LL has partners[] and projects[]; easiest for the detail page to consume.
Flat entries JSON - One top-level partners[] and projects[], each item lists its ll_slugs; better if the same partner/project appears in multiple LLs.
Two files - partners.json and projects.json; explicit separation, but a bit more plumbing.
Data authoring model.question: What shape should that file have?
Data authoring model.answer: Use one separate static JSON file grouped by Living Lab slug, with each LL containing partners[] and projects[].

options_presented: Data + Sync - Author in data/, have sync.py copy it to app/public/data/; follows the existing pipeline-app contract.
App Public Only - Author directly in app/public/data/; fewer steps, but breaks the established source/published-copy pattern.
Generated Later - Define the contract now but leave the actual file generation to a future import/data-management phase.
Data authoring model.question: Should this file be hand-authored directly in data/, or should data-pipeline/sync.py also publish it into app/public/data/ like other static runtime data?
Data authoring model.answer: Author the grouped JSON under data/, and have data-pipeline/sync.py publish it to app/public/data/.

options_presented: Separate lazy fetch - Keep it separate and fetch partners_projects.json only when the tab is active; avoids bloating core LL metadata.
Merge into LL metadata - sync.py copies/merges it into ll_metadata.json; easier one-fetch app model, but the metadata file grows.
Eager separate fetch - Keep a separate file, but load it at page startup with LL metadata; simpler state once loaded.
Data authoring model.question: Should the app load this as part of ll_metadata.json, or fetch it separately only when the tab is used?
Data authoring model.answer: Keep it separate and fetch partners_projects.json only when the Partners & Projects tab is active.

options_presented: Confirmed Partners Only - Show only partner/institution locations that have permission to be displayed; safest and matches the feedback caveat.
Partners + Exemplar Projects - Show both partner locations and project/example locations when coordinates are available.
Projects Only - Treat partners as overview-panel content, and use the map only for project/example sites.
Freeform: show partners only on the map, assume all entries in the JSON have permission to be displayed.
Map point behavior.question: What should appear as points on the map?
Map point behavior.answer: Show partners only on the map, and assume every partner entry present in the JSON has permission to be displayed.

options_presented: Tooltip + Link - Hover/focus shows partner name; click opens the partner website when available. Matches the feedback note about hover links.
Select In Panel - Click/hover highlights the matching partner card in the panel; website link lives in the card.
Tooltip Only - Marker shows name/type/location but does not navigate anywhere from the map.
Map point behavior.question: What should a partner marker do when clicked or hovered?
Map point behavior.answer: Partner markers show a tooltip on hover/focus, and clicking a marker opens the partner website when available.

options_presented: Base Map + Boundary Only - Reuse the Leaflet base map and LL boundary outline/mask, with no thematic raster/vector layer or legend.
Reuse Default Landscape Layer - Show the landscape raster behind partner points; richer context, but the tab becomes visually tied to one data theme.
Configurable Background Later - Build the tab so the background can later switch between base/landscape/other layers, but ship base-only now.
Map point behavior.question: What map background/overlay should this tab use?
Map point behavior.answer: Use the Leaflet base map plus LL boundary only, with partner point markers. Do not render a thematic raster/vector layer or thematic legend on this tab.

options_presented: List Only - Partners without coordinates still appear in the Partners section, but not on the map.
Hide Entire Entry - Partners without coordinates are omitted from both map and panel.
Use Approximate LL Center - Place them at the LL centroid with a visual approximate cue.
Map point behavior.question: How should missing coordinates be handled?
Map point behavior.answer: Partners without coordinates still appear in the Partners section, but do not render on the map.

options_presented: Name, Type, Location, Website - Compact and realistic for a first hand-authored dataset.
Name, Type, Location, Website, Short Description - More informative, but adds bilingual authoring work.
Name, Contact, Location, Website - Contact-oriented, but risks exposing individual details.
Overview panel content.question: What fields should a partner entry show?
Overview panel content.answer: Partner entries show name, type, location, and website.

options_presented: Title, Summary, Website - Lightweight exemplar-project cards; enough context without becoming a project database.
Title, Summary, Partner, Website - Adds a relationship to the partner section, useful if projects should explain who is involved.
Title, Summary, Status, Duration, Website - More like a project catalogue; richer but more authoring overhead.
Overview panel content.question: What fields should a project entry show?
Overview panel content.answer: Project entries show title, summary, partner, and website.

options_presented: Bilingual Text Fields - Labels/types/summaries use { en, de } fields where language matters; URLs stay shared.
Shared Names Only - Names/titles/types are shared strings; only project summaries are bilingual.
English First - Author English fields now and allow German fallbacks until content is translated.
Overview panel content.question: Should partner/project names and descriptions be bilingual?
Overview panel content.answer: Use shared strings for partner names, project titles, and partner/project type labels; only project summaries are bilingual. URLs remain shared.

options_presented: Quiet Empty State - Show a short bilingual No partners/projects listed yet message in the relevant section.
Hide Empty Section - If there are no partners or projects, hide that section entirely.
Coming Soon Badge - Keep the section visible with a coming soon tone.
Overview panel content.question: What should the empty state say when a Living Lab has no partners or no projects authored yet?
Overview panel content.answer: Show a short bilingual "No partners/projects listed yet" message in the relevant empty section.
